title: Bounded-below site comparison
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme and $\Lambda$ a finite discrete ring, with left module sheaves and the coefficient categories of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. The inverse image of the comparison morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] is fully faithful on the bounded-below derived categories:
$$
\nu_T^*:\Dplus(T_{\Et},\Lambda)\longrightarrow\Dplus(T_{\Proet},\Lambda).
$$
More precisely, the unit of its adjunction with the bounded-below right derived direct image is a natural isomorphism
$$
\operatorname{id}\xrightarrow{\sim}R\nu_{T,*}\nu_T^*.
$$
No constructibility or finiteness of the individual module sheaves is assumed.

proof.text: Specialize the canonical comparison adjunction to A = ModuleCat Λ. The comparison inverse image is additive and exact, direct image is additive and left exact, and both sheaf categories are Grothendieck abelian with enough injectives. The ordinary comparison unit is invertible by [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-grothendieck-unit], so each of its components at injective objects is invertible.

For every injective etale sheaf I, apply [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-grothendieck-injective-acyclicity] to obtain that its comparison inverse image is direct-image acyclic. Apply the existing proved generic criterion [lem-cbc-derived-unit-injective-acyclicity] with this fact and the ordinary-unit isomorphism. It proves invertibility of the derivedPlus unit at each bounded-below object. This criterion implements the same bounded-below injective-resolution argument of the source, including the acyclic comparison calculation.

The existing equality Adjunction.derivedAdjunctionPlus_eq_derivedPlus identifies the restricted unbounded adjunction used in the statement with the directly constructed bounded-below adjunction used by the criterion. Rewrite by this equality. NatTrans.isIso_iff_isIso_app assembles the pointwise invertibility into invertibility of the specified natural transformation. Its asIso is therefore the comparison isomorphism. Full faithfulness is the usual consequence of invertibility of the adjunction unit (Adjunction.fullyFaithfulLOfIsIsoUnit).
